title: Mount Polley tailings storage facility breach: undetected foundation stratum, undrained failure, and post-breach tailings standards
summary: Mount Polley is encoded as a tailings-storage failure where design/site characterization failed to identify the critical Upper GLU foundation layer and susceptibility to undrained failure; the record keeps inspection/regulatory conclusions and technology/independent-review recommendations distinct.

status_history.note: Added as rev0026 impoundment/tailings failure lane record.

place.location: Mount Polley Mine, British Columbia, Canada

subjects.name: Independent Expert Engineering Investigation and Review Panel
Williams Lake Indian Band and Soda Creek Indian Band

claims.claim: The Mount Polley panel site says an independent review panel of three geotechnical experts was established on August 18, 2014 to investigate the August 4, 2014 TSF breach and delivered its final report and recommendations on January 30, 2015.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The panel report states that the breach occurred in the Perimeter Embankment early on August 4, 2014, that loss of containment was sudden with no warning, and that the pond elevation recorded the evening before was 2.3 m below the crest.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The panel narrowed the mechanism away from human intervention and overtopping and toward foundation failure, identifying Upper GLU as a controlling stratum and undrained failure as the viable hypothesis.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The panel concluded that the dominant contribution to the failure resided in design: the design did not account for the complex foundation environment, and investigations/site characterization failed to identify a continuous GLU layer and its susceptibility to undrained failure under embankment stresses.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The panel’s future-facing conclusion called for improved adoption of best applicable practices and migration to best available technology, including filtered/unsaturated/compacted tailings and independent tailings review boards.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

sequence_of_events: Sudden perimeter embankment breach; loss of containment without warning; post-breach expert investigation compared hypotheses and focused on foundation-layer behavior.
type_payload.proximate_cause: undrained failure in undetected Upper GLU foundation layer under embankment load
contributing_factors: foundation investigations/site characterization missed continuous GLU layer
design did not account for complex subglacial/pre-glacial foundation environment
inspection/regulator conclusions differ from design conclusions
latent_conditions: foundation material-state hidden from design/review surface
tailings facility lifecycle governance and independent review not enough to guarantee state legibility

handling_notes: Preserve casualty and community dignity; avoid spectacle and avoid using disasters as clever engineering anecdotes.
Separate physical mechanism, design/construction/operation history, monitoring or warning limits, regulatory/governance context, and post-event correction rails.
